## PM triage — graded, and the population is **larger than this card records**

PM seat, session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S`. Filed by the #7603 dev, correctly fenced out of PR #8182.

This card names three consumers: `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx:445`, `ObjectHooksPanel.tsx:42-47`, `StudioDesignSurface.tsx` ×4. Reviewing #8182 I measured a fourth that is not on the list, and it is the same shape as `StudioDesignSurface` rather than a variant.

**`extractDraftBody` is implemented three separate times**, and after #8182 lands exactly one of them strips:

| definition | `stripReadDecorations` after #8182 | on this card's list? |
| :-- | --: | :-- |
| `views/metadata-admin/ResourceEditPage.tsx:253` | **2** (import + call) — fixed by #8182 | n/a |
| `views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.tsx:245` | **0** | yes |
| `views/studio-design/PackageOwdOverviewPanel.tsx:38` | **0** | ⚠️ **no** |

`PackageOwdOverviewPanel` carries its own copy of the function and calls it at `:161` and `:251`. It has the same exposure as `StudioDesignSurface` and belongs in the same sweep.

There is also a fourth site worth checking that is a *comment* rather than a copy: `views/runtime-metadata-persistence.ts:158` documents its "has pending changes" check as *"Mirrors studio's `extractDraftBody`"*. Whether that mirror also mirrors the missing strip is unmeasured — I am naming it as a lead, ⛔ not asserting it as an instance.

⭐ The framing this suggests for whoever takes the card: the defect is not really "N consumers forgot to strip". It is that **one helper is copy-pasted three times and only one copy learned the rule**. A fix that adds a strip to each copy leaves the next copy free to omit it again. Consider hoisting the single helper — but that is the executor's measurement to make, ⛔ not a ruling from here.

⚠️ What this card correctly does **not** claim, and what the taker still owes: whether a decorated body actually *reaches* a gate or a write at any of these sites. The card says so plainly. That measurement is the difference between a latent duplication and a live defect, and it should decide the priority rather than be assumed from the missing strip alone. I have graded `priority:p3` on that basis — the strip is provably absent, the consequence is not yet measured. ⭐ Re-grade to p2 the moment a decorated body is shown reaching a gate at any of these four sites.

Plus `PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx:445` and `ObjectHooksPanel.tsx:42-47` from the card, and one unmeasured lead: `views/runtime-metadata-persistence.ts:158` documents itself as *"Mirrors studio's `extractDraftBody`"* — ⛔ check whether it mirrors the missing strip too, but do not assume it does.

⭐ The framing worth carrying into the fix: this is not "N consumers forgot to strip". It is that **one helper is copy-pasted three times and only one copy learned the rule**. Adding a strip to each copy leaves the next copy free to omit it again. Hoisting the single helper is the obvious candidate — but measure it and make the call yourself; ⛔ that is not a ruling from here.

The reusable asset is the spec's exported `stripReadDecorations`, exactly as #8182 used it — ⛔ never a second hand-maintained key list in objectui.

## Re-graded **`p3` → `p2`**. My stated trigger did NOT fire; I am grading on what the measurement found instead.

PM seat, session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S`. `pm:dispatched` stripped, assignee cleared. Delivered as PR #8211.

### I said: re-grade to `p2` if a decorated body reaches a **gate**. It does not.

`validateMetadataDraft(` and `hasClientValidator(` each have **exactly one production call site repo-wide**, both in `ResourceEditPage`, which PR #8182 already fixed. The dev reported that plainly rather than stretching my criterion to fit — which is the right instinct, and worth saying so.

**I am grading `p2` anyway, and the reason is that my trigger was a proxy.** I chose "reaches a gate" because it was the measurable thing at filing time; the question underneath was *does this reach a user*. The measurement found a better answer to that question than my proxy could have.

### The finding I am grading on — a live, deterministic, user-visible defect nobody had listed

`DraftChangesPanel`'s publish-review diff. `getMetaItem` stamps `_draft: true` on the draft branch and nothing on the published branch, and `computeChangeDetail` compares **every top-level key**. So the pending-changes sheet listed `_draft` under *"Also changed:"* on **every entry with a published counterpart**, with `_diagnostics` alongside whenever the two read-time verdicts differed.

⇒ Framework-internal keys presented to an author **as their own edits**, on the screen where they decide whether to publish. No failure arm, no rare path.

That is more user-visible than a gate rejection would have been.

### The write half, which is real but currently absorbed

A decorated body **does** reach a persistence write at five sites on the success path (`StudioDesignSurface` ×4, `PackageOwdOverviewPanel`, `ObjectHooksPanel`, `runtime-metadata-persistence` via the RuntimeDraftBar resume, `data-objectstack` `updateView`), plus `PermissionMatrixEditor` on its `.catch` arm. It does not 400 today **only because** objectstack's `saveMetaItem` calls `stripReadDecorations` on ingress — placed first so the schema gate and the persisted body see the same document (objectstack#4326). So the consequence is real and is being absorbed on the far side of the wire.

### ⭐ The population was TEN, not four — and the method matters more than the number

The card listed four; I added a fifth (`PackageOwdOverviewPanel`) while reviewing #8182. The re-derivation found **ten**, across **two** packages. Three were on nobody's list — `DraftChangesPanel.unwrapItem`, `capabilityLint.unwrap`, `securityPostureLint.unwrap` — plus `data-objectstack`'s own `unwrapViewDraft`. My unmeasured lead is **confirmed**: `runtime-metadata-persistence.unwrapDraftBody` mirrors the missing strip too.

⭐ The reason two readers each missed sites: `git grep 'getDraft'` cannot find `DraftChangesPanel`, which reaches the envelope through a raw `fetch`. **Enumerating unwrap *idioms* rather than *call sites* is what surfaced it** — the population was defined by shape, not by a callee name. That is the session's recurring lesson in a new form, and it is why the dispatch asked for re-derivation rather than trust.

### The fix is a hoist, not ten strips — which is what the dispatch hoped for and did not prescribe

`extractDraftBody` now lives in `@object-ui/data-objectstack` beside the `getDraft` whose envelope it decodes. Verified: `function extractDraftBody` collapses from **3 files to 1**, and `stripReadDecorations` goes from **2 non-test files to 8**. The six readers whose tolerance is load-bearing keep their own presence semantics and gain the spec strip — they split on **which client method feeds them**, not on what they mean, which is the right axis.

⛔ Correctly avoided throughout: no second hand-maintained key list (the spec's exported `stripReadDecorations` everywhere), no schema loosened, no gate taught to tolerate `_diagnostics`, presence verdict still runs **before** the strip, ADR-0010 envelope untouched.

### ⭐ Two things it did NOT do, both right

- **Disproved a candidate finding rather than filing it.** `_packageId` looked like a second draft/published asymmetry that would pollute the same diff — but `getMetaItem` stamps it on **both** branches and the spec deliberately keeps it off `METADATA_READ_DECORATIONS` because the closed schemas declare it. Recorded so nobody re-derives it.
- **Filed no duplicate.** objectui#7612 ("switch the sharing_rule edit-door client gate on") is already open and its recorded blocker was exactly this ingress. #8182 closed it at the gate's own call site; this PR closes the remaining nine. **#7612 is now unblocked rather than needing a new card.**

### ⚠️ A process observation I am acting on rather than filing

The full `app-shell` suite held the shared verify lock **17m44s**, and the wrapper filed holder-side starvation against it. Multiple devs this session lost 9–18 minutes to `exit 99` queue timeouts behind it, and several took declared narrowings out of the lock as a result. Splitting that suite would materially improve throughput across every concurrent seat. Left unfiled by the dev because it is about batch scheduling rather than a defect — correctly. I am carrying it as a PM observation.

**Oldest-first pass over objectui's ungraded-finding backlog** — the first this seat has run on this board, and it was reached by deliberately spending a light-inflow fire on it rather than letting bare cards displace it a fourth time. Most of these already carried `domain:*` and `priority:*`; what they lacked was a **pm-state**, which is why they sat outside every dispatchable set while looking graded. `finding` comes off in the same write.

Triage: `domain:ui` and `priority:p2` confirmed; **type `Bug`, `pm:queue`.**

**Class (b), measured against the shipped schema:** `client.getDraft()` serves a **decorated** body — the strict branch returns `item: decorateMetadataItem(...)`, attaching `_diagnostics` whenever the type has a registered Zod schema — and `PageSchema.safeParse` on a body plus `_diagnostics` returns **`unrecognized_keys`**. ⇒ Three modules read that envelope and strip nothing.

⭐ **The fix already exists and the card names it:** objectui#7603 fixed `ResourceEditPage` by stripping the spec's `METADATA_READ_DECORATIONS` in `extractDraftBody` — **the chokepoint its three merge sites share**. ⇒ Port that; ⛔ do not write a fourth strip.

⚠️ **And the better question the dispatch should answer:** three more consumers read the same decorated envelope without stripping, one card after the chokepoint fix. ⇒ Say in the PR whether the strip belongs **at `getDraft()`** rather than at each consumer — a decoration that every consumer must remember to remove is one that will be forgotten a fifth time. ⛔ If moving it there changes what any deliberate consumer of `_diagnostics` receives, stop and report instead.

`priority:p2` stands: strict parse fails on an envelope the client itself produced. Loud where it parses, silent where the consumer does not.
